Divisive

/dih-VY-siv/ — stress on VY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Divisive describes something that causes strong disagreement and splits people into opposing sides.

Pineapple on pizza is the most divisive question in our entire cafeteria.

Worked Example

The new school dress code became divisive when half the students supported it and half protested loudly.

Divide (split into parts) + -ive (inclined to): the dress code has the quality of splitting the student body. More precise than 'unpopular' because divisive captures the sense of creating opposing sides rather than just being disliked.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

contentious: causing heated, quarrelsome argument

controversial: provoking strong public disagreement

polarizing: pushing people to opposite extremes

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

uniting: bringing people together as one

conciliatory: meant to calm disagreement and restore peace

Where it sits · how badly it splits people apart — debatable → controversial → contentious → divisive

debatable vs. divisive: A debatable idea invites polite discussion; a divisive one splits people into angry camps.

controversial vs. divisive: 'Controversial' stirs strong opinions, but divisive actually breaks a group into opposing sides.

contentious vs. divisive: A contentious topic sparks heated argument; a divisive one leaves lasting rifts between people.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — divis-

Root — divis-: shifted stem of divide — from Latin dividere, 'to split apart' (past participle divisus) (Latin)

Suffix — -ive

Suffix — -ive: having the quality or tendency of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Divide swaps its -de ending for -s- before -ive: inclined to divide people into opposing sides. Its math-flavored relative divisible ('can be divided') is a different word — numbers are divisible; arguments are divisive.

Use the root in a new word: indivisible

Use the root in a new word: indivisible: The pledge describes the nation as indivisible — impossible to split apart.

Word Choice

formal

Reach for divisive when something creates a clear split between people into opposing camps. It's stronger than 'unpopular' or 'controversial'—divisive implies fundamental disagreement that breaks communities apart.
